$schema: See scripts/audit-check.mjs. Every entry needs a reason and a reviewBy date.
$policy: Exceptions are deferrals, not pardons. An entry is only justified when the advisory cannot be fixed without a breaking upgrade AND the exposure does not reach a shipped build or a user's device. Anything reachable from the app bundle gets fixed, not listed.

allow.reason: Quadratic replacement of percent-encoded runs. This one is in the bundle: expo-router reads every link's query with query-string 7.1.3, which requires decode-uri-component ^0.2.2. The fixed 0.5.1 is ESM only, which query-string 7's require() cannot load, and npm's only other route is expo-router 58, a new Expo SDK. So it is fixed in place instead: patches/decode-uri-component+0.2.2.patch swaps in 0.5.1's single-pass decoder and keeps 0.2.2's API. npm audit reads only the version, so it still reports 0.2.2. scripts/__tests__/decode-uri-component-patch.test.ts fails if the patch stops applying. Remove this entry when expo-router stops depending on query-string 7.
Exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input; on a long enough link, 0.2.2 overflows the stack. Fixed by the same patch as GHSA-qr28-fpjm-wq7f; see that entry.

Memory exhaustion when validating an oversized array against a schema with no length limit. The repo's own zod, which eslint-plugin-react-hooks uses, is on 4.6.7 and patched. What remains is the zod 3.25.76 nested under @expo/cli, which validates the CLI's own config and API responses on a developer's machine or in CI; the app does not import zod and it is not in the bundle. The fix is 4.6.6, a major version away from the 3.x API @expo/cli is written against, and 3.25.76 is the last 3.x release, so this waits for Expo to move to zod 4.
